ransomware.context: A document next to a padlock, showing files that have been locked until a ransom is paid. Used for malware warnings, security incident pages and cyber attack reports.

phishing.context: A fishing hook dangling over an envelope, standing for fake emails that try to trick people into giving up details. Used in security training, spam filters and fraud warnings.

computer-worm.context: A monitor with a row of round segments arching over its top edge like a worm crawling out. Used for malware types, self-spreading infections and antivirus alerts.

keylogger.context: A keyboard with an open eye above it, showing that every keystroke is being watched. Used for spyware warnings, monitoring tools and password theft awareness.

botnet.context: Four small bot heads at the corners linked to a central computer in a hub network. Used for explaining zombie networks, DDoS sources and command and control servers.

brute-force-attack.context: A sledgehammer swinging down onto a padlock. Used for password cracking, login attempt limits and security log entries about repeated guesses.

sql-injection.context: A database cylinder with a syringe pushed into its side. Used for web application attacks, input validation warnings and security scan results.

zero-day.context: A calendar page with a large zero on its face and a small bug at its corner. Used for unpatched vulnerabilities that attackers know about before a fix exists.

backdoor.context: A server tower with a swung-open door beside it, standing for hidden access that bypasses normal login. Used for trojan warnings and unauthorised remote access reports.

honeypot-trap.context: A honey pot with a drip, fed by a network line with two nodes. Used for decoy systems that lure attackers so their methods can be studied.

air-gap.context: Two monitors linked by a cable that has a clear gap in the middle. Used for isolated networks, offline machines and high security separation.

vulnerability.context: A shield with a jagged crack running down through it. Used for security weaknesses, scan findings and exposed or broken protection.

security-patch.context: A shield with an adhesive bandage stuck diagonally across it. Used for security updates, hotfixes and fixing known weaknesses.

penetration-test.context: A shield with an arrow piercing through it. Used for ethical hacking exercises, red team work and testing how well defences hold.

threat-radar.context: A round radar screen with rings, a sweep line and a blip on one ring. Used for threat detection dashboards and live monitoring of suspicious activity.

threat-hunting.context: A magnifying glass with a crosshair on its lens. Used for actively searching systems for hidden attackers and investigating suspicious activity.

bug-bounty.context: A beetle on top of a stack of coins. Used for programmes that pay people for responsibly reporting security flaws.

man-in-the-middle.context: Two computers linked through a hooded figure standing between them. Used for interception attacks where someone secretly sits on a connection.

email-spoofing.context: An envelope above a half face mask, standing for a message that fakes its sender. Used for impersonation warnings and email security settings.

malicious-usb.context: A USB flash drive with a skull drawn on its body. Used for warnings about infected or rigged drives and device control policies.

juice-jacking.context: A public charging port box with a cable plugged in and two dark eyes above the socket. Used for warnings about untrusted charging stations that can steal data.

data-breach.context: A database cylinder split by a jagged crack with bits spilling out. Used for leak notifications, incident reports and stolen data alerts.

data-exfiltration.context: A database behind a brick wall with an arrow carrying data up and over the wall. Used for data theft through covert transfers out of a network.

privilege-escalation.context: A figure standing on the top step of a staircase holding a key up. Used for gaining higher access rights than allowed, admin takeovers and permission reviews.

packet-sniffer.context: A network line carrying small packets with a magnifying glass over them. Used for capturing and inspecting network traffic.

session-hijacking.context: A cookie gripped from above by a clawed grabber. Used for stolen login sessions and account takeover through captured cookies.

blocklist.context: A banned symbol beside a list of entries. Used for deny lists of blocked users, addresses, domains or words.

ad-blocker.context: A browser window with an ad banner struck through. Used for extensions and settings that stop adverts and pop-ups from loading.

onion-routing.context: An onion bulb with layered rings inside. Used for layered, multi-hop anonymous networks that hide who is talking to whom.

dictionary-attack.context: An open book with a key rising from its pages and two speed lines. Used for password guessing from word lists.

hardware-security-module.context: A flat rack-mounted box with status lights and a key on its front. Used for dedicated hardware that stores and guards encryption keys.

passkey.context: A person silhouette with a small key at its lower right. Used for passwordless sign-in tied to a person and a device.

magic-link.context: An envelope with a chain link on its front and a sparkle at its corner. Used for one-click email sign-in links that need no password.

password-generator.context: A six-sided die with a pip on its top face and a curved arrow beside it. Used for creating random strong passwords on demand.

voice-id.context: Sound waveform bars framed by four corner scan brackets. Used for voice recognition and speaker verification.

palm-scan.context: An open palm with a scan line across it inside corner brackets. Used for palm and hand based biometric entry and payment.

hardware-security-key.context: A slim USB security key seen from above with a connector, a round touch button and a keyring hole. Used for physical two-factor login devices.

backup-codes.context: A sheet with two columns of short dashed codes and a small key at its top. Used for printable recovery codes for two-factor accounts.

security-token-fob.context: A keychain token with a small display window, a button and a loop for a key ring. Used for older one-time-password devices that show a changing code.

push-authentication.context: A smartphone showing a notification with a check button and a cross button. Used for approve or deny sign-in prompts sent to a phone.

access-key-fob.context: A teardrop-shaped key fob with a ring hole and three contactless wave arcs. Used for tap-to-enter door fobs and proximity keys.

biometric-padlock.context: A padlock with a fingerprint whorl on its body instead of a keyhole. Used for fingerprint-locked items, apps and smart locks.

fingerprint-terminal.context: A wall-mounted reader with a small screen above a fingerprint pad. Used for time clocks and door readers that use a finger.

access-card-reader.context: A wall card reader with a card held against it and wave arcs between them. Used for badge and swipe card door entry.

identity-verification.context: An ID card beside a face inside scan brackets. Used for checking that a person matches their identity document.

id-card-scan.context: An identity card inside camera frame brackets. Used for scanning or photographing an ID document.

age-verification.context: An ID card with a photo mark and the number 18. Used for age gates and checks for adult-only content or purchases.

account-recovery.context: A life ring buoy with a person in its centre. Used for getting back into a locked or lost account.

key-switch.context: A round panel switch with a key in the centre slot and two position marks. Used for keyed on and off controls and ignition style switches.

door-release-button.context: A wall plate with a large round push button and a small doorway mark above it. Used for push-to-exit buttons beside secured doors.

full-height-turnstile.context: A tall revolving cage with a central post and bars between fixed side grilles. Used for high security entry gates in stations, stadiums and plants.

cipher-wheel.context: Two concentric rings with tick marks between them and a pin in the centre. Used for letter-substitution decoders and puzzle ciphers.

rotor-cipher-machine.context: A boxy cipher machine with three rotors on top and keys on the front. Used for historic mechanical encryption and codebreaking stories.

scytale.context: A rod with a paper strip wound around it in a slanted spiral. Used for the ancient transposition cipher of wrapped message strips.

key-exchange.context: Two keys facing each other with two opposed arrows passing between them. Used for swapping keys to set up an encrypted channel.

end-to-end-encryption.context: A chat bubble with a padlock inside it. Used for messages that only the sender and receiver can read.

certificate-chain.context: Three small certificates stepping down a diagonal and linked together. Used for chains of trust from a root authority to a website.

invisible-ink.context: A sheet with faint dotted lines and a small flame under its corner revealing solid text. Used for hidden messages that appear when treated.

steganography.context: A picture with mountains and a sun and a magnifier over its corner revealing text lines. Used for data hidden inside ordinary images.

one-time-pad.context: A tear-off notepad with a torn top edge and rows of short code groups. Used for the unbreakable pad cipher with single use keys.

split-key.context: A key broken into three separate pieces laid along a diagonal. Used for secret sharing where several parts are needed to rebuild a key.

face-blur.context: A head and shoulders with the face filled by a checker of square pixels. Used for pixelating faces to hide a person's identity in photos and video.

redacted-document.context: A document page with text lines, two of them replaced by thick solid bars. Used for censored or blacked-out sensitive text.

data-masking.context: An input field showing four bullet characters followed by plain characters. Used for partly hiding values such as card or account numbers.

privacy-screen.context: A laptop whose screen is covered in vertical louver lines. Used for filters that stop people beside you from reading your display.

webcam-cover.context: A laptop camera lens half covered by a small sliding shutter. Used for blocking the camera when it is not in use.

faraday-pouch.context: A phone poking out of a pouch beside signal arcs crossed by a slash. Used for bags that block radio signals to phones and keys.

signal-jammer.context: A small box with four antennas and a zigzag line above it. Used for devices that block or disrupt radio and phone signals.

rfid-blocking-wallet.context: A wallet with a card slot line and a small shield on its front. Used for wallets that protect contactless cards from skimming.

tracking-cookie.context: A cookie with chips and a small open eye in its middle. Used for third-party cookies that follow people across websites.

location-tracking.context: A map pin with an eye in its head and a dotted trail behind it. Used for apps and devices that follow where a person goes.

app-permissions.context: A dialog box with a small camera at the top and two buttons below, one wide and one narrow. Used for prompts asking to allow access to the camera or other features.

data-protection.context: A database cylinder with a shield at its lower right. Used for safeguarding stored data and privacy compliance.

digital-footprint.context: A bare footprint with a row of toes and a few square pixels trailing behind it. Used for the traces people leave behind online.

data-erasure.context: A person silhouette whose lower half is being rubbed out by an eraser, with crumbs falling. Used for deleting personal data and the right to be forgotten.

disappearing-message.context: A chat bubble whose right side dissolves into dots, with a small timer at its corner. Used for chats that delete themselves after a set time.

drive-destruction.context: A hard drive with a hammer striking its top and a crack across its face. Used for physically destroying storage so data cannot be recovered.

secure-shredding-bin.context: A locked wheelie bin with a document slot in its lid and a padlock on the front. Used for office bins where paper is collected for secure shredding.

parental-control.context: A small child figure standing in front of a large shield. Used for family settings that protect children online.

item-tracker-tag.context: A small rounded tag on a key ring with a key, and signal arcs above the tag. Used for Bluetooth trackers that help find lost keys and bags.
